excerpts.speaker: Zellnor Myrie
excerpts.short_exact_quote: we need to invest in permanent homes
excerpts.notes: Full answer supports permanent housing, supportive-housing accountability, vouchers, rental relief, and replacing shelter spending with permanent homes.
excerpts.attribution_notes: Quote is from the candidate answer following question 10 answer in the body-verified NYC Mayor questionnaire.
excerpts.claim_summary: Zellnor Myrie supports permanent Housing First or supportive housing paired with services for people experiencing homelessness.

excerpts.speaker: Brad Lander
excerpts.short_exact_quote: connect people to housing with services
excerpts.notes: Full answer explicitly supports a Housing First model with supportive housing and wraparound services, alongside asylum legal and employment assistance.
excerpts.attribution_notes: Quote is from the candidate answer following question 10 answer in the body-verified NYC Mayor questionnaire.
excerpts.claim_summary: Brad Lander supports permanent Housing First or supportive housing paired with services for people experiencing homelessness.

excerpts.speaker: Michael Blake
excerpts.short_exact_quote: invest in permanent and supportive housing
excerpts.notes: Full answer supports permanent and supportive housing, mental-health and social services, humane shelters, and culturally competent community partnerships.
excerpts.attribution_notes: Quote is from the candidate answer following question 11 answer in the body-verified NYC Mayor questionnaire.
excerpts.claim_summary: Michael Blake supports permanent Housing First or supportive housing paired with services for people experiencing homelessness.

excerpts.speaker: Scott M. Stringer
excerpts.notes: Full answer supports Housing First, stable housing paired with services, and citywide supportive-service expansion.
excerpts.attribution_notes: Quote is from the candidate answer following question 11 answer in the body-verified NYC Mayor questionnaire.
excerpts.claim_summary: Scott M. Stringer supports permanent Housing First or supportive housing paired with services for people experiencing homelessness.

excerpts.speaker: Zohran Kwame Mamdani
excerpts.short_exact_quote: As an assemblymember I have both visited incarcerated New Yorkers, drawn public
excerpts.notes: Candidate answer to: 17. Do you commit to visit constituents who are incarcerated? Will you work to secure the release of individuals who have demonstrated sincere remorse, worked toward rehabilitation and are not deemed a threat to society? Full answer retained in source body; the short anchor is interpreted only in that context.
excerpts.attribution_notes: Quote is from the candidate answer following question 17 answer in the body-verified NYC Mayor questionnaire.
excerpts.claim_summary: Zohran Kwame Mamdani supports engagement with incarcerated constituents and review or release for people demonstrating rehabilitation.

excerpts.speaker: Zohran Kwame Mamdani
excerpts.short_exact_quote: The best way to address homelessness is by providing people with lasting homes
excerpts.notes: Full answer supports Housing First, supportive and affordable housing, rent freezes, rental assistance, tenant protections, shelter rights, and coordinated services.
excerpts.attribution_notes: Quote is from the candidate answer following question 11 answer in the body-verified NYC Mayor questionnaire.
excerpts.claim_summary: Zohran Kwame Mamdani supports permanent Housing First or supportive housing paired with services for people experiencing homelessness.

excerpts.speaker: Jessica Ramos
excerpts.notes: Full answer emphasizes rent freezes and affordability as homelessness prevention; this is compatible with but distinct from Housing First supportive-housing implementation.
excerpts.attribution_notes: Quote is from the candidate answer following question 22 answer in the body-verified NYC Mayor questionnaire.
excerpts.claim_summary: Jessica Ramos supports a rent freeze as an affordability and homelessness-prevention measure.

excerpts.speaker: Adrienne E. Adams
excerpts.short_exact_quote: help people stay in their homes and avoid homelessness
excerpts.notes: Full answer emphasizes CityFHEPS implementation, housing vouchers, shelter exit, and guaranteed income for youth and families.
excerpts.attribution_notes: Quote is from the candidate answer following question 11 answer in the body-verified NYC Mayor questionnaire.
excerpts.claim_summary: Adrienne E. Adams supports implementing housing-voucher laws and income supports to prevent and exit homelessness.

comparisons.interpretation: Mamdani and Zellnor Myrie both support permanent or Housing First/supportive housing rather than relying on shelter or incarceration. Their full answers differ in agency coordination, services, vouchers, and implementation details.

Mamdani and Brad Lander both support permanent or Housing First/supportive housing rather than relying on shelter or incarceration. Their full answers differ in agency coordination, services, vouchers, and implementation details.

Mamdani and Michael Blake both support permanent or Housing First/supportive housing rather than relying on shelter or incarceration. Their full answers differ in agency coordination, services, vouchers, and implementation details.

Mamdani and Scott M. Stringer both support permanent or Housing First/supportive housing rather than relying on shelter or incarceration. Their full answers differ in agency coordination, services, vouchers, and implementation details.

Mamdani emphasizes Housing First and supportive/permanent housing for people already experiencing homelessness; Ramos emphasizes a rent freeze as upstream affordability and homelessness prevention. Neither source opposes the other mechanism.

Mamdani emphasizes Housing First, supportive housing, rent relief, and service coordination; Adams emphasizes implementing CityFHEPS voucher laws and guaranteed-income support to prevent and exit homelessness. Neither source opposes the other mechanism.
